_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

Reviewed head `8189e214720e18de9236907b9c5d4cf8c2518392` against the current `main`, with a fresh read of the PR, its reviews/comments (none), and the linked issues #18505 and #18004 (both open, both carrying `ready-for-dev` and `priority:low`).

Scope: this is Canvas presentation in `src/components/features/chat/components/context-window-meter.tsx` plus its theme-contrast test. It owns the popover surface and tone maps, so it belongs in `OpenHands/OpenHands`; no server, wire-contract, or persisted-state surface is touched.

What I verified on the head:
- The tone maps now resolve from the same semantic roles the sibling Usage drawer (`usage-panel/context-meter.tsx`) already uses: `text-feedback-warning`/`text-feedback-error` for labels and `bg-feedback-warning`/`bg-status-error` for fills. No new palette token is added; per-theme overrides (Light+, Solarized Light, DeepSea) are inherited.
- The popover is now `bg-surface-raised`, which matches the surface the contrast test already measured (`--oh-surface-raised`), so the test and the rendered backdrop are consistent instead of measuring a surface the component did not use.
- The bar keeps its 6px height (`h-1.5`); the 1px `border` with `borderColor: CONTEXT_WINDOW_TRACK_COLOR` adds the full-range boundary without growing the bar, and the absolutely-positioned fill (`inset-y-0 left-0`) sits inside the padding box, so the boundary stays visible under the fill.
- The diff only extends the existing five-theme checks (adds `--oh-foreground` to the fill-vs-track loop and a composited boundary check); no assertion is removed or weakened.

Evidence and CI: authenticated local Agent Server 1.55.1 + real `deepseek/deepseek-flash` before/after GIF, MP4, and a five-theme PNG are linked and are appropriate for a static-render color change; the latest `Validate PR description`, `CI / test-and-build (ubuntu)`, and `test-and-build (windows)` check runs on this head are green. The `release ready` `startup_failure` is not head-specific: every recent run of that reusable workflow fails at startup across unrelated branches.

Focused tests in the workspace: `__tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx`, `context-window-ring.test.tsx`, `context-window-meter.test.tsx`, and `usage-panel/context-meter.test.tsx` plus the surrounding chat/usage/theme suites: 118 passed, 38 of them the directly-scoped color/ring/meter files.

Acceptance criteria checklist (issue #18505):
- [x] Warning/danger labels meet 4.5:1 on the popover surface in all five themes (asserted against `--oh-surface-raised`).
- [x] Neutral, warning, and danger fills meet 3:1 against the track; the full-range boundary meets 3:1 against the popover surface (composited check).
- [x] Tones resolve from semantic feedback roles; no shared palette token added or modified.
- [x] Thresholds (70%/90%), ring, compaction, and Usage navigation unchanged; existing handlers and tests still pass.
- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run build` gates are green on this head in CI.
- [x] Theme contract in `__tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx` covers the popover surface and its boundary.

Non-blocking, already disclosed by the author: the change moves the popover backdrop from `--oh-color-tertiary` to `--oh-surface-raised`, which slightly improves (but does not fix) the unrelated muted-text contrast in Solarized Light; issue #18505 scopes muted text and the ring's fixed amber/red arc out of this change, so this is not a merge gate.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, architecture, or evidence gaps found.

✅ APPROVED

_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

Presentation-only change to `src/components/features/chat/model-messages.tsx` (+11/-11) that replaces fixed Tailwind neutral palette classes with the repository's semantic theme roles. Scope is Canvas-owned (UI presentation), the change follows the dependency direction, and it needs no Agent Server/SDK contract work. No material correctness, security, compatibility, or architecture defect found.

**What I verified on head `e71b4499fa721f67ced214d83b22452d469ecb83`**

- Diff is confined to the one component; event anchoring, expansion, profile switching, diagnostics rendering, free-model display, and the shared `GenericEventMessage` wrapper are untouched (only className strings changed).
- Every replacement resolves to an existing token declared in `src/tailwind.css` (`border-border`, `text-text-tertiary`, `text-contrast`, `bg-surface-raised`, `hover:bg-interactive-hover-low`), so no raw hex/neutral utility remains in the file.
- I recomputed WCAG contrast from the shipped palettes in `src/themes/color-theme/definitions/*` against the real chat surface (`conversation-main` renders the chat panel as `bg-canvas-base`): profile name and titles (`text-contrast`) 12.25:1 to 16.29:1; expanded diagnostics and the info icon (`text-text-tertiary`) 4.99:1 on Light+/Solarized chat and 4.65:1 on the hover surface; switch chip (`text-contrast` on `bg-surface-raised`) 12.39:1 or better; the closest value is Solarized Light, which still clears the 4.5:1 text and 3:1 icon targets. Hover resolves to the theme's own `interactive-hover-low`, so light themes no longer paint a dark neutral surface.
- Focused tests pass locally: `__tests__/components/features/chat/model-messages.test.tsx`, `__tests__/components/conversation-events/chat/messages-model-messages.test.tsx`, and `__tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx` (19 passed).
- Current head checks: `test-and-build (ubuntu)` and `test-and-build (windows)` success, `pr-title`, `Validate PR description`, and `check-pr-artifacts` success; `live-e2e` and manifest jobs are skipped as designed for a PR (they run post-merge). Linked issue #18509 is open with `bug`, `priority:low`, `ready-for-dev`; parent #18004 remains open. No prior review from this account on this head.

**Acceptance-criteria checklist (issue #18509)**

- [x] Names, diagnostics, titles, and switch chip meet their contrast targets in all five shipped themes on the rendered chat/hover/chip surfaces (recomputed from the palette definitions; Solarized Light is the tightest and still passes).
- [x] Switch info icon meets the 3:1 UI-icon target in all five themes (>=4.65:1).
- [x] Border and row hover resolve to semantic roles (`border-border`, `hover:bg-interactive-hover-low`); no dark neutral hover in light themes.
- [x] No `shadcn/no-raw-colors` hits remain in the changed file and no new allow entries were added to `eslint.config.js`.
- [x] Event anchoring, expansion/collapse, `/model <name>` switching, the diagnostic readout, the `(free)` suffix, and the empty-profile hint are behaviorally unchanged (covered by the passing focused tests).

Evidence: the PR supplies before/after media, a five-theme comparison, a hover comparison, and a video captured in the real Canvas against a real local backend, with provenance for computed colors, which satisfies the functional-change evidence rule. The change affects no prompts, tool selection, conversation payloads, or evaluation paths, so there is no eval risk.

No blocking or non-blocking findings to report.

✅ APPROVED

## Review: PR #18510 — fix(theme): keep model profile messages readable

Fresh review of head `e71b4499fa721f67ced214d83b22452d469ecb83` (matches the PR head).

**Scope.** The change is a presentation-only batch of #18004 in `src/components/features/chat/model-messages.tsx`, fully owned by this repository (Agent Canvas UI). It correctly stays within the linked issue's declared scope: the shared `GenericEventMessage` wrapper and its outer muted chevron are untouched.

**Correctness.** Every replacement maps to a real semantic theme role defined in `src/tailwind.css` `@theme inline` (`text-contrast`, `text-text-tertiary`, `border-border`, `bg-interactive-hover-low`, `bg-surface-raised`), all backed by `--oh-*` tokens in `:root` and the five theme definitions. A nonexistent class would silently no-op, so I verified each one resolves. Only `className` strings changed; no logic, state, or anchoring behavior is affected.

- Row border `border-neutral-700` to `border-border`; `hr` border likewise.
- Row hover `hover:bg-neutral-700` to `hover:bg-interactive-hover-low` (`#F2F2F2` in Light+, `#F5EEDB` in Solarized Light, `cool-grey-900` in dark themes), removing the dark hover surface on light palettes.
- Name / titles / chip text `text-neutral-200` to `text-contrast` (`#1F1F1F` Light+, `#002B36` Solarized Light, `#FFFFFF` default dark), fixing the ~1.26:1 name contrast.
- Diagnostics, empty-profile hint, row chevron, switch info icon (`text-neutral-300`/`text-neutral-400`) to `text-text-tertiary` (`#4D4D4D` Light+, `#586E75` Solarized Light).
- Switch chip `bg-neutral-800` to `bg-surface-raised`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [x] Names, diagnostics, icons, titles, and chips follow all five shipped themes and meet contrast targets — token values support the reported AFTER measurements (diagnostics >=4.99:1, icons >=4.65:1, chips >=12.39:1), with before/after captures linked in the PR and issue.
- [x] Borders and hover use semantic theme roles; no raw palette classes remain in the component, and no `shadcn/no-raw-colors` allowlist exception was added to `eslint.config.js`.
- [x] Event anchoring, expansion, switching, diagnostics, and free-model display are unchanged (CSS-only diff).

**Evidence and checks.** This is a small localized CSS fix (LOW risk), so no design doc is required. The PR supplies real-app before/after captures, a five-theme comparison, and a hover comparison with measurement provenance. CI on the exact head is green (`test-and-build` ubuntu and windows success; lint/typecheck covered). Locally I ran the focused suites — `get-event-content.test.tsx`, `syntax-highlighter-themes.test.ts`, `terminal-themes.test.ts` — 107 passed. No test asserts the replaced class strings, so no regression path is broken.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, or architecture findings. This is a cosmetic accessibility fix with appropriate evidence.

✅ APPROVED

reviews.body:
_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

## Review summary

Scope check: this is a Canvas presentation change to the shared `BrandButton` (`src/components/features/settings/brand-button.tsx`), which is owned by `OpenHands/OpenHands`. It replaces fixed red palette classes with existing theme roles; no SDK, automation, or wire contract is involved. Belongs here.

### What the change does

- `danger`: `bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700` -> `bg-feedback-error text-contrast-foreground hover:bg-feedback-error/90`
- `ghost-danger`: `text-red-600 ... hover:text-red-700` -> `text-feedback-error ...` (underline/hover:no-underline preserved)

### Verification on the current head (`f52f2f7b`)

- Re-fetched the mutable state: head SHA still matches, PR is open, label `type: fix`, no existing reviews or review threads, linked issues #18512 (`bug`, `priority:low`) and #18004 (`ready-for-dev`) unchanged.
- Check runs for the exact head are green (ubuntu/windows test-and-build, PR-description, artifact checks).
- Ran the focused tests in the workspace at this head: `brand-button`, `delete-profile-modal`, and `color-themes` - 31 passed. `color-themes.test.tsx` re-derives the `--oh-feedback-error` contract per theme, which is the behavior this PR relies on.
- Recomputed WCAG contrast from the shipped tokens for all five themes:
  - filled normal: neutral/neo 6.62, DeepSea 7.47, Light+ 5.86, Solarized Light 5.61
  - filled hover (feedback-error at 90% over the modal surface): neutral/neo 5.70, DeepSea 6.40, Light+ 5.13, Solarized Light 4.91
  - ghost label on the card surface: neutral/neo 5.14, DeepSea 5.45, Light+ 5.28, Solarized Light 4.94
  All >= 4.5:1, matching the PR's stated figures.

### Design notes (non-blocking)

Using `--oh-contrast-foreground` as the filled label ink is a sound pick: it is dark in the dark themes and light in the light themes, so it clears 4.5:1 on `--oh-feedback-error` everywhere. The danger-specific `--oh-danger-foreground` fallback in the dark themes is near-white, which would not clear the threshold on the light-red feedback surface, so avoiding it is correct.

### Acceptance checklist

- [x] Four raw red classes replaced with existing semantic roles; still visibly destructive (red surface).
- [x] Destructive labels >= 4.5:1 on normal and hover backgrounds in all five shipped themes (computed above).
- [x] Variants, disabled state, handlers, and confirmation/deletion flow untouched; only the two destructive class strings changed.
- [x] No API, stored-state, translation, or lint-severity change.
- [x] Existing relevant tests and CI pass on the exact head; before/after media attached in the PR.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, or architecture findings.

✅ APPROVED

reviews.body:
_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

## Review: PR #18515 — fix(theme): keep launch errors and retry readable

**Scope:** `src/routes/launch.tsx` is Agent Canvas frontend presentation, owned by this repository. The change is confined to two `className` swaps; no API, state, i18n, theme-token, or dependency changes. Scope gate passes. Linked issue #18514 carries `bug`, `priority:low`, `ready-for-dev`; parent #18004 is `enhancement`, `priority:low`, `ready-for-dev`.

**Head verified:** `6e1abb6408d2568160dae51f8cf2fb64e69e72e9`, no existing reviews or review comments, no failing check runs on the head.

### What changed

- Error heading: `text-red-400` → `text-feedback-error` (existing readable error-text role, `--oh-feedback-error`, per `specs/form-feedback.md` FF-001 / `@spec MCP-004`).
- Try Again: `bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700` → `bg-contrast text-contrast-foreground hover:bg-contrast/90`. This mirrors the established `contrast`/`contrast-foreground` action-role pair already used in `src/components/features/sidebar/sidebar-onboarding-checklist-item-preview.tsx`.

### Verification

I recomputed sRGB contrast against the real rendered `bg-surface` card from the shipped theme tokens:

| Theme | Heading (`feedback-error` on `surface`) | Old `red-400` baseline |
|---|---|---|
| openhands-deepsea | 5.45:1 | — |
| openhands-neutral | 5.14:1 | — |
| openhands-neo | 5.14:1 | — |
| light-plus | 5.28:1 | 2.49:1 |
| solarized-light | 4.94:1 | 2.26:1 |

All five themes clear the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold (20px medium is below the large-text threshold); the two light themes were the failing ones and now pass. Try Again label contrast, including the composited `bg-contrast/90` hover fill over the card surface, is ≥ 10.7:1 normal and hover in every theme.

**Focused tests in the workspace (node 24, committed `package-lock.json`):**
- `vitest run __tests__/routes/launch.test.tsx __tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx` → 2 files, 50 tests passed. This covers parsing, parameter rendering, trust, creation and navigation/failure paths, plus the FF-001/WN-001 theme contrast contract.
- `grep` confirms no raw palette utilities (`red-*`, `blue-*`, `text-white`, arbitrary hex) remain in `src/routes/launch.tsx`.
- Head CI: `test-and-build (ubuntu)`, `test-and-build (windows)`, `check-pr-artifacts`, and the PR-title/description validators all report `success`; zero failing check runs.

### Acceptance criteria (from #18514)

- [x] Heading meets 4.5:1 on the actual card surface in all five themes (ratios above).
- [x] Try Again uses existing semantic roles only; no raw palette utilities remain; label meets 4.5:1 normal and hover across themes.
- [x] Behavior/layout unchanged: only `className` strings differ; Go Home still navigates to `/conversations`, Try Again still calls `window.location.reload()`, trust requirement, error copy, ARIA, and layout untouched.
- [x] Focused route and theme tests pass.

Non-blocking note: the PR body claims `npm run lint` passes with 0 errors; I could not reproduce a full `eslint` run in this review sandbox (the process was OOM-killed under the default heap), so I relied on the green Ubuntu/Windows `test-and-build` checks and the focused Vitest runs. That does not change the verdict.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, architecture, or evidence gaps found. The change is a minimal, correctly-scoped migration to existing semantic theme roles, backed by per-theme contrast math and a real running-app before/after capture.

✅ APPROVED
